title: Lair in its own scene
eyebrow: Your ask on 2026-10-29: the Lair and the Market in their own scene, so the raid's scene can be cleared and reset cleanly

short.lead: Today the Lair and the Market are two rooms inside RaidScene (the one scene that holds the whole game). They sit 1000 m and 1100 m off to the side, and you get between them and the castle by teleport. Nothing in the game loads a scene. So a raid's castle, its broken walls and its debris live in the same scene as the Lair, and only code we remember to write cleans them up. A co-op check showed the problem: after a raid ended, all 63 rooms, 214 breakable parts and 434 debris effects were still loaded behind the Lair on both machines. I've fixed that one case (the castle now clears as you arrive back), but you're right that the real fix is separate scenes. This page shows how I'd split them and gives you three choices to make.
short.hint: Tap an item to see what I found in the code, or what you need to pick.
items: RaidScene holds the network manager, the game state, the event manager, the Lair (with the ledger, century dial, strongbox and portal), the Market (counters, haul landing) and the raid (castle generator, loot and guard spawners, the Ophan, extraction). RaidSceneRooms.cs puts the Lair and the Market in place, and RoomTravel teleports join them. PurrNet, the networking library, has a scene module, but nothing uses it. The OphanGym, the Ophan test level, is built as a copy of RaidScene.

Purses, debt and the haul pile are saved per save slot (LairHubManager, HaulPileSave) and restored when the server starts. That makes a split safe: the Lair can be rebuilt from the save, so nothing in it has to stay inside the raid scene.

Five places look up an object that would end up in the other scene: the century dial finds the Lair hub, the strongbox finds the Lair hub, the haul landing finds the raid director, a market counter finds the haul landing, and the raid director finds the castle lockdown. Each needs a link that survives the split, such as a static registry (a shared list the object adds itself to) or an event, instead of a search of the scene.

Option A in the first choice ("How should the scenes split?") is my suggestion: a small Bootstrap scene that is never unloaded (network, game state, events, players), with the Lair scene and the Raid scene loaded on top of it, one at a time, by PurrNet so both machines switch together.
Pick under Choices, in "How should the scenes split?"

Loading a scene causes one long frame, which shows as a hitch. Your rule is no hitches, so my suggestion (option A in the second choice) loads the next raid scene in the background while you are in the Lair and switches at the portal.
Pick under Choices, in "When should the raid scene load?"

choices: split
How should the scenes split?
A
Bootstrap plus Lair plus Raid

A Bootstrap scene stays loaded the whole session and holds the network, game state, events and the players. The Lair scene and the Raid scene are loaded on top of it, one at a time, by PurrNet's scene module so both machines switch together. Returning from a raid unloads the raid scene, so everything in it goes, whatever spawned it. Players are never despawned, so co-op never reconnects.
B
Two scenes, swapped whole

The Lair scene and the Raid scene each hold their own copy of everything and replace each other completely. Simplest to set up, but players, the network session and anything carried are torn down at every switch and must be rebuilt, which risks the co-op session and carried loot.
C
Lair stays, raid in its own scene

RaidScene keeps the Lair and the Market, and only the castle and its spawners move to a raid scene loaded on top. The smallest change, but the Lair still shares a scene with the network and game state, so it is not the full separation you asked for.
A gives the clean reset you asked for without touching the co-op connection. B resets even more but tears down the session each time. C is half the job.
load
When should the raid scene load?
A
In the background while you're in the Lair

The next raid scene loads quietly while you stand in the Lair, inactive, and is switched on at the portal. No long frame anywhere, at the cost of holding the raid scene in memory while you're in the Lair.
B
At the portal, behind a short fade
The raid scene loads when you step into the portal, behind a fade to black of about a second. Less memory in the Lair, but there is a load pause each time.
Your rule is steady frames over memory, so A.
gym
What happens to the Ophan Gym?
A
A raid-scene variant loaded with the same Lair
The gym becomes a raid scene of its own (the Ophan comes 30 s in), loaded through the same Lair and portal as a real raid, so the gym tests the real flow.
B
Stays one combined test scene
The gym keeps the Lair inside it as today. Faster to start, but it no longer tests the real Lair-to-raid flow.
A keeps the gym honest.

wrapup.summary: The Lair and the Market move to their own scene, with a small Bootstrap scene underneath, and a raid unloads its whole scene on return. Today's leak (a whole castle left loaded behind the Lair) is already fixed for that one case.
wrapup.changing: Nothing about scenes changes until you pick. The fix for the leftover castle and the frame-pacing work are already on the branch AjsAgent/gym-with-demand-page.
wrapup.blocking: Your three picks: how the scenes split, when the raid scene loads, and what happens to the Ophan Gym.
wrapup.next: I open a GitHub issue for the split, with one sub-issue for each step. Then I build it on this branch and check it in co-op: set out on a raid, break walls, die, return, and count that nothing of the raid is left loaded on either machine.
